title: How STRC lost its par: The timeline behind Strategy's preferred-stock meltdown
summary: Title: A look at how falling Bitcoin prices, capital structure changes pushed STRC below $83 in just five weeks. URL Source: https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/06/20/how-strc-lost-its-par-the-timeline-behind-strategy-s-preferred-stock-meltdown Published Time: 2026-06-20T13:00:00.000Z Markdown Content: Jun 20, 2026, 1:00 p.m. 4 min read ![Image 1: Strategy Executive Chairman Michael Saylor at the Digital Asset Summit in New York City on March 20, 2025. (Nikhilesh De)](https://www.coindesk.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.sanity.io%2Fimages%2Fs3y3vcno%2Fproduction%2F3a6393eb4ae1f1db4ef1caec0023161c16707226-6000x3376.jpg%3Fauto%3Dformat&w=3840&q=75) Strategy Executive Chairman Michael Saylor. (Nikhilesh De) Summary * Strategy's preferred stock STRC, designed to hold a price of $100, on Thursday dropped to a low of $83. * A number of events led up to the slide, including a buyback of convertible notes at an 8% discount and rival Strive saying it would start paying a daily dividend on its SATA equivalent. * The decline was also driven by a combination of falling bitcoin prices, reduced liquidity buffers and weakening investor confidence. STRC, the dividend-paying preferred equity issued by bitcoin treasury company Strategy (MSTR), is designed to hold a price of $100, its par value. It doesn't always work that way. On Thursday, the stock price dropped below $83, some 17% below the target and the lowest since it debuted in July 2025. The security is meant to be high-yield, low-volatility. Keeping the stock near par is critical because it allows Strategy to raise capital efficiently through at-the-market (ATM) offerings to fund the annualized 11.5% payout. In recent weeks, however, a sharp decline in the price of bitcoin [BTC$64,147.98](https://www.coindesk.com/price/bitcoin), combined with a series of management decisions, have pushed STRC significantly below its intended trading level.
